sentences.text: Koreanosaurus was a small dinosaur from the Orodrominae subfamily that lived in South Korea during the Late Cretaceous.
This animal measured between 2 and 2.4 meters in total body length.
Unlike most of its relatives in the Orodrominae group, Koreanosaurus is assumed to have lived on all fours as a quadruped.
Three specimens were discovered in 2003 in the Seonso Conglomerate near the Bibong-ri dinosaur egg site on the southern coast of the Korean Peninsula.
The species was named Koreanosaurus boseongensis to honor the Boseong site 5 where the fossils were found.
The genus was first described in a 2008 master's thesis by Dae-Gil Lee and officially published in 2011 by a team including Min Huh and Pascal Godefroit.
Researchers believe Koreanosaurus was a burrowing dinosaur based on its close relatives and fossil evidence of small burrows found in the same geological layer.
Modern phylogenetic analyses consistently classify Koreanosaurus as a member of the family Thescelosauridae within the subfamily Orodrominae.
Some researchers have suggested that Koreanosaurus might belong to the family Jeholosauridae or be closely related to it, though this is debated.
